answer: The design passes a stress test on the coldest day with one doublet tripping. The unmet heat is 0 MW, and the backup boiler (18 MW) covers the demand. The system survives with no unmet heat or cooling. [F16]

user: Why not use 2500 m wells with a heat pump instead of drilling to 3100 m?
answer: Using 2500 m wells with a 10 MW heat pump delivers 75.07 GWh/yr of heat [F29] vs. 110.7 GWh/yr at 3100 m [F15]. The 3100 m design has 44.13 EUR/MWh LCOE [F22] and 2,990 t CO₂/yr [F22], while the 2500 m design has 53.57 EUR/MWh LCOE [F29] and 4,909 t CO₂/yr [F29]. The 3100 m design provides 47% more heat and 60% lower emissions. A heat pump at 2500 m is not cost-effective here.
